transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-04-14
Time: 16:00 PST
Duration: ~45 min
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Ari Morales (CTO, VectorSearch), Priya Singh (ML Engineer), Ben Lowe (Infra)
Links referenced: security doc (link sent after call), benchmark template: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/vec-rerank-2025 (note: placeholder)

[00:00] Maya: ok going to get started, thanks everyone for joining, we're going to do a perf and cost deep dive for embeddings + rerank, sound good?
[00:08] Ari: yeah thanks, we've got Priya and Ben here, we'll be mainly focused on production rerank, latency SLOs around 50ms p95 ideally, and cost per q, so curious what tradeoffs you recommend
[00:18] Samir: awesome, quick agenda: vector dims memory/cpu tradeoffs, batching and throughput, where caching helps (embedding cache vs kv cache), quantization options, and then deployment sizing (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private/vpc)
[00:30] Priya: one quick data point - our current embedding dim is 1536, about 100k vectors, qps steady at 20 with spikes to 100 for short periods, retrieval topk 100 then we rerank top 10 with a cross-encoder
[00:45] Maya: perfect, that helps; two patterns we'll consider: 1) late-stage rerank with cross-encoder (more expensive per query) and 2) approximate retrieval + cheap re-score. Cost math changes a lot depending on dim and batch.
[01:05] Ben: question, for private deployment we'll need VPC peering and specific firewall rules, also prefer no egress on vectors, is that supported?
[01:12] Samir: yes, Redwood Private supports customer managed VPC and private control plane; we can pin to on-prem too, network constraints may increase lat slightly but we can size clusters accordingly
[01:25] Priya: about caching - I sometimes hear "KV cache" in Redwood docs - isn't that for autoregressive models? Does it help for rerank?
[01:33] Samir: good call, KV cache is mostly for generative decoders, for reranking it's different. What helps is caching computed candidate embeddings and precomputing cross-encoder features if you have stable candidate sets. We call it "embedding cache" more often in retrieval flows; apologies for mixed terminology in some notes
[01:50] Ari: ok makes sense. If we precompute candidate embeddings of 100k vectors at 1536 dims, what's the memory footprint roughly?
[01:58] Samir: rough calc: 1536 dims * 4 bytes (float32) ~ 6 KB per vector? wait math - 1536*4 = 6144 bytes ~6 KB, times 100k ~ 600 MB, actually 600 MB, plus indexing overhead (HNSW or IVF) so plan for ~1.2-1.5 GB depending on index type. If you quantize to float16 that's half, int8/4bit further reduces but affects similarity fidelity for some models
[02:30] Priya: we'd like to try 768 dim models too - tradeoff on accuracy vs speed?
[02:35] Samir: yes 768 dims cut memory roughly in half and improves throughput; but often drop in recall/rdoc depends on your prompt/test set. We typically recommend running evals on your holdout. For approximate numbers - 768 dims can be ~1.7-2x faster in CPU-bound nearest neighbor search and ~2-3x cheaper in serving cost if compute-bound
[02:55] Ari: what about batch sizes? currently we batch queries 16 for embeddings, and rerank runs single-shot cross-encoder scoring for top10 - is there room to batch rerank?
[03:05] Samir: yes you can batch cross-encoder scoring; if your model supports batched forward passes you can amortize overhead. For cross-encoders batch sizes of 8-32 often sweet spot on GPU; but latency SLO and p95 matters - larger batch increases average throughput but can increase tail latency. For 50ms p95 we recommend small batches (8) and cheaper quantized models or allocate more dedicated GPUs with lower batch latency
[03:30] Priya: curious about quantization: int8 or 4-bit - how safe is it for rerank accuracy?
[03:36] Samir: in our tests int8 typically has minimal impact for many transformer encoders; 4-bit (Q4) can have more variance, but with calibration and per-channel quant (and using higher-dim intermediate layers as fp16) we often get acceptable results. We advise running A/B evals. Redwood Optimize can suggest quant profiles per model and workload. Also note some runtimes might not support fast kernels for certain quant formats on older GPUs
[03:58] Ben: any rules of thumb for cost: hosted vs dedicated vs private for 100 qps with these workloads?
[04:05] Maya: rough ballpark: Hosted (multi-tenant) often simplest but costs more per q. Dedicated reserved capacity is best if you have steady load (commits), could be 40-60% cheaper at scale. Private/on-prem eliminates cloud infra fees but adds ops and often higher initial sizing cost. We'll produce a more precise estimate given your qps, model dims, and rerank complexity
[04:30] Ari: ok, can you walk through a sample cost calc for 20 qps steady with spikes?
[04:36] Samir: simple example: embeddings encoder at 10ms per query batched (assume batching amortized), rerank cross-encoder for top10 at 25ms per q on a GPU (batched). So total ~35ms avg. For 20 qps that's 700ms of GPU compute per second - not a direct mapping but you need e.g. 1 GPU with capacity and headroom. For spikes to 100 qps we recommend autoscale/burst or an additional Dedicated pool for burst capacity. Cost-wise hosted could be $X/tokenish, but we'll send a tailored estimate - (note: numbers intentionally high level)
[05:10] Priya: what's the impact of increasing top-k retrieval from 100 to 500 on rerank cost?
[05:15] Samir: rerank cost scales linearly with number of candidates if you rerank all with cross-encoder. One strategy: use light-weight re-ranker to narrow to 50 then full cross-encoder on top10. So cost = embed retrieval cost + re-ranker cost + cross-encoder cost. For large k, consider approximate rerank pipelines or pre-filtering to avoid 5x cost increase
[05:40] Ari: tail latency, p95 vs p99 - we see occasional 200-300ms tails, what's typical mitigation?
[05:47] Samir: tail often from CPU-gc, node autoscaling, or cold kernels; solutions: pinned nodes for low-latency workloads, warmed kernels (no cold start), smaller batch sizes, and KV/prefix caches for stable subrequests. Also use LB routing to favor low-latency capacity tiers (e.g., dedicated small-GPU nodes) and circuit-breakers for fallback to smaller models when tails spike
[06:10] Ben: for private on-prem, what about GPU types - A10G vs A100? how much difference?
[06:16] Samir: A100 gives better throughput, especially for bigger models and mixed precision. A10G is cost-effective for many embedding models and mid-sized cross-encoders. Kernel support matters - some quant kernels run faster on newer architecture. We'll propose a sizing table: A10G for cost-conscious, A100 for high throughput and lower tail latency
[06:34] Priya: can Redwood run our benchmark on your infra or do we need to run it?
[06:38] Maya: we can run it if you give sample vectors and queries; Samir will share the benchmark config. We usually run a 1-hour run with variable qps and capture p50/p95/p99 and cost breakdown. Priya: ok we'll share data
[06:52] Samir: for benchmarks we'll vary vector dims (768/1536/3072), batch sizes (8/16/32/64), and quantization (fp32, fp16, int8). We'll also test rerank strategies: full cross-encoder vs two-stage re-ranker.
[07:08] Ari: any gotchas on indexing? HNSW parameters can affect recall vs latency - do you tune efConstruction/efSearch?
[07:15] Samir: yes those params are critical; higher efSearch increases recall but also increases query time. We'll record that in bench results. Also consider IVF + PQ for very large corpora to reduce memory footprint but with some recall tradeoffs
[07:30] Priya: about storage for embeddings - do you recommend storing raw float vectors in S3 + index in memory on serve nodes?
[07:37] Samir: common pattern: store original floats in object store for durability, load dense index into memory on serve nodes. For very large corpora load shards or use disk-backed indices. For low-latency we keep active working set in memory and cold shards on disk
[07:58] Ari: security questions quick: audit logs, KMS, SSO?
[08:03] Maya: Redwood Private supports KMS/HSM integrations, audit logs, RBAC and SSO/SAML; we'll send SOC2 docs after call
[08:12] Ben: ok thanks, sample benchmark and security docs then we'll reconvene
[08:18] Maya: quick note on quantization accuracy checks - we recommend running quality evals on your labeled queries. Redwood Optimize can track regressions and alert on drift
[08:28] Priya: ok one more: what latency target is realistic for p95 if we target 10ms? seems aggressive
[08:33] Samir: 10ms p95 for rerank is very aggressive for cross-encoder on GPU - more realistic for a lightweight re-ranker or embedding-only retrieval. For cross-encoder you'd be looking at 20-50ms p95 with careful tuning and dedicated GPUs; 10ms requires highly optimized server infra or distilled/smaller models
[08:55] Ari: any specific configurations to recommend for our 100k / 20 qps baseline with spikes to 100?
[09:01] Samir: start with Dedicated pool (1-2 A10G) sized for steady 20 qps plus autoscale for spikes, run 1-hour bench with dims 1536/768, try int8 and fp16, batch cross-encoder at 8, and set p95 target at 50ms; if p99 tails are bad add pinned capacity or switch to A100 for lower tail
[09:28] Priya: perfect. Also can you share example cost sheet?
[09:32] Maya: we'll produce an initial cost sheet after bench - includes per-1M-query cost estimates for hosted vs dedicated vs private
[09:41] Ari: thanks, i'm concerned about accuracy regression when quantizing - how do you measure that?
[09:46] Samir: measure on labeled holdout: recall@k, MRR, and business metrics. Redwood Optimize can run evals and flag delta beyond threshold; we also recommend shadow runs for a week before switching
[09:58] Ben: about networking for private: we have strict egress rules, won't allow internet-facing endpoints, will need private peering
[10:05] Maya: that's supported, we have on-prem patterns and private control plane options. Samir will take infra notes
[10:12] Priya: any example results you can share now? even ballpark numbers for 1536 dim cross-encoder cost per q?
[10:18] Samir: ballpark: cross-encoder on A10G batched at 8 ~ 15-30ms per example depending on model size; cost per q depends on batching and cluster utilization; we'll run exact numbers in bench
[10:33] Ari: ok let's summarize next steps
[10:36] Maya: recap: 1) Priya to share sample 100k vectors + query distribution by 2025-04-16; 2) Redwood to run bench and return p50/p95/p99 and cost breakdown by 2025-04-18; 3) Samir to schedule on-prem sizing call with Ben by 2025-04-20; 4) Maya to send SOC2 & security docs by 2025-04-16; 5) Redwood to deliver Dedicated vs Hosted cost estimate by 2025-04-17
[11:05] Priya: agree, thanks everyone
[11:08] Ari: thanks, appreciate the thorough walkthrough
[11:11] Maya: thanks all, we'll follow up in email and post the benchmark template
